qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Dominant slot holdings at Heathrow and Madrid provide hub-and-spoke feed advantages, but airline passenger capacity is shopped on price aggregators. Multi-cycle ROIC averages only 5-8% (failing the 12% hurdle), with volatile cash flows vulnerable to jet fuel price spikes, pilot union wage pressures, and cyclical economic downturns.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (Reject – G3 Moat & Pricing). Anglo-Spanish airline group controlling British Airways and Iberia. Despite dominant slot positions at London Heathrow and Madrid-Barajas, IAG operates in a capital-intensive, cyclical industry. 10-year average ROIC lands in the 5-8% range (below the 12% hurdle), burdened by heavy fleet capex, aggressive labor unions, volatile jet fuel costs, and zero durable pricing power across full cycles.
qualitative.evidence: Over a full 10-year cycle, IAG's ROIC averages 5-8%, dragged down by massive pandemic-era equity dilution/losses and severe cyclical troughs, despite strong post-pandemic recovery years (17-18% in 2024-2025). The business remains a price-taker on core economy cabins, facing intense competition from low-cost carriers on short-haul and US legacy carriers on transatlantic routes, alongside high fixed aircraft lease and fuel obligations.
